title: Sony Is Giving You a Reason to Party With $100 Off One of Our Favorite Speakers
author: Les Shu
text: All products featured on WIRED are independently selected by our editors. However, we may receive compensation from retailers and/or from purchases of products through these links. Learn more.Sony’s ULT speakers are at their lowest price ever. These outdoor party speakers are some of the best-sounding you’ll find, and include options like the ULT Tower 7 (our pick for deejaying) and the ULT Field 7 (our pick for best compact party speaker).Whether it’s tunes for a backyard party, an impromptu karaoke session with friends, or announcements during a kids’ softball game, one of these Sony speakers is more than capable of handling the job.For more speaker recommendations, check out these guides for the Best Party Speakers, Best Bluetooth Speakers, and Best Computer Speakers.Sony ULT Tower 7 for $548 ($102 Off)Photograph: Chris HaslamPhotograph: Chris HaslamSonyULT Tower 7$650 $548 (16% off) Best Buy$650 $548 (16% off) AmazonSony offers several party speakers to choose from, but we like the ULT Tower 7 because it hits the sweet spot in sound quality, price, and features—especially if you fancy yourself a DJ, thanks to its multiple inputs and Bluetooth. It pumps out 420 watts of sound output, enough for a small stage. With a 30-hour battery life, it can run from day to night. Plug in a mic, and you have got a makeshift PA system for your soapbox.The bass might not rival a club, but your body will feel it when Kendrick Lamar’s “HUMBLE.” comes on. Our reviewer Chris Haslam wishes it had a retractable handle. It’s also heavy and big, so it isn’t something you want to move around often.Other Sony ULT Speaker DealsCourtesy of AmazonCourtesy of AmazonSonyULT Tower 5$450 $348 (23% off) Amazon$450 $348 (23% off) Best BuyCalling this the baby brother of the Tower 7 is a bit misleading—it’s just as big. It has a 300-watt output, which is plenty for indoor and outdoor use. It has the same wired and wireless connectivity as the Tower 7, but it costs $200 less during the sale. Note that it only has 20 hours of battery life, so make sure there’s a power outlet nearby if you plan to go long.Most PopularGearOnlyFans Creators Are Pissed That Meta Lets Muse Talk DirtyBy Reece RogersGearHere’s Exactly How Tesla Made Its New 230-Mph Car ‘Fly’By Jeremy WhiteDealsGet Your Kitchen Thanksgiving-Ready With All-Clad’s Factory Seconds SaleBy Kat MerckGearThis New Food Delivery App Could Be the Antidote to Menu MarkupsBy Reece RogersPhotograph: Chris HaslamPhotograph: Chris HaslamPhotograph: Chris HaslamSonyULT Field 7$500 $448 (10% off) Amazon$500 $448 (10% off) Best BuyThe ULT Field 7 is our pick for the best compact party speaker. Compared to its Tower siblings and other party boxes, it certainly is. Reviewer Chris Haslam calls it the ideal speaker for a dorm or apartment that you can take outdoors. For a speaker of this size, it has great sound and bass. Its IP67 rating means it resists dust and water and can even handle a quick accidental dip in the pool. Besides Bluetooth, there are inputs for a mic or guitar. It’s not the biggest discount, but you can save a little over $50.Courtesy of Best BuyCourtesy of Best BuySonyULT Tower Max$1,500 $1,198 (20% off) Best BuyThis is for when you want to crank the dial to 11. It has everything that the Tower 7 has plus more. It is huge, heavy, and needs to be plugged in to work, but it can output 2,150 watts, which, quite frankly, is scary. It wouldn’t be out of place in a small club, but it might have your neighbors calling the police.
